decisions.title: model_was_loaded is derived from file existence instead of actual load success, silently skipping training
decisions.reason: Verified against the patch: after the load attempt, when load_model fails it leaves model None and the `if model is None:` branch executes `q, gs_result = find_latent_dim(...)` (and init_model), so q becomes non-None. The later `model_was_loaded = (checkpoint_path and checkpoint_path.exists() and q is not None)` therefore evaluates True purely because the checkpoint file still exists on disk, even though a fresh untrained model was created. `should_train = config.autoencoder_training and not model_was_loaded` then evaluates False, so training is skipped and the untrained model flows downstream. The logic is genuinely derived from file existence rather than load success; the only dependency is that load_model returns (None, None) on failure (rather than raising), which is strongly implied by the code's own 'If model not loaded, find latent dim and initialize new model' path guarded by an exists() check. The finding follows from the changed code.

decisions.title: Checkpointing is silently re-enabled by defaulting to out_dir/model.pt, making results depend on out_dir reuse
decisions.reason: The patch unconditionally sets `checkpoint_path = Path(config.out_dir) / 'model.pt'` when config.checkpoint_path is falsy, and the preceding block does `if checkpoint_path and checkpoint_path.exists(): model, q = load_model(...)`. Combined with the training-skip logic (should_train = autoencoder_training and not model_was_loaded), a second run into the same out_dir will find the previously written checkpoint and skip training, so training-affecting settings (n_epochs, lr, h_dim) or same-width changed input are silently ignored. This behavior does follow from the patch; the one unverifiable element is that the (unshown) save block writes to this same checkpoint_path, which is strongly implied by the default and by the candidate's cited `save_model(model, str(checkpoint_path), q)`. The statefulness risk is real, so confirmed, though confidence is moderated by the unseen save code and the possibility the default was intentional.
